findings.body:
`middleware.RequireRole("admin")` wrapped both handlers on the base branch; this diff drops that wrapper and registers bare `http.HandlerFunc`s on the new `/api/v2` subrouter. There is no `v2.Use(...)`, no per-route `authz(...)`, and no other file in the tree that re-applies the admin check.

**Failure mode:** any caller that can hit the server may invoke `GET /api/v2/admin/users` and `POST /api/v2/admin/roles` without an admin role — user enumeration and role mutation become unauthorized.

Restore the guard on the subrouter or each route, for example:

```go
authz := middleware.RequireRole("admin")
v2 := r.PathPrefix("/api/v2").Subrouter()
v2.Handle("/admin/users", authz(http.HandlerFunc(a.listUsers))).Methods("GET")
v2.Handle("/admin/roles", authz(http.HandlerFunc(a.editRoles))).Methods("POST")
```

(Verified against base `fff74f2` `routes.go` and full tree listing — only this file exists; nothing else supplies the missing authz.)

Same regression as `/admin/users`: `POST /api/v2/admin/roles` is now `http.HandlerFunc(a.editRoles)` with no `middleware.RequireRole("admin")` wrapper.

**Failure mode:** unauthenticated or non-admin clients can mutate roles. Re-wrap with the same `authz` helper used on the base branch (or `v2.Use(authz)` if the middleware signature allows).

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — this change strips admin authorization from privileged endpoints while relocating them under `/api/v2`.

## Narrative

The PR title and comment describe a PathPrefix subrouter cleanup for API versioning. The path move itself is coherent (`/admin/*` → `/api/v2/admin/*`), but the diff also deletes `authz := middleware.RequireRole("admin")` and registers `listUsers` / `editRoles` as bare `http.HandlerFunc` values.

On the base revision both handlers were wrapped with `authz(...)`. Nothing in this tiny repo re-applies `RequireRole` on the new subrouter (no `Use()`, no per-route middleware, no other files). After merge, `GET /api/v2/admin/users` and `POST /api/v2/admin/roles` are reachable without the admin role check that previously gated them.

That is a broken-authorization regression on user-listing and role-editing surfaces — treat it as blocking for any environment where this router is mounted.

Secondary note (not filed inline): callers still on `/admin/users` and `/admin/roles` will 404 unless a redirect or dual-register compatibility shim is added elsewhere. Coordinate the path cutover separately from restoring auth.

## Release decision

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: Base routes.go wrapped both admin handlers with middleware.RequireRole("admin"); head drops that wrapper and registers bare HandlerFuncs on /api/v2 with no v2.Use or other RequireRole anywhere in the tree, so the privileged endpoints are unauthenticated.
Base registered POST /admin/roles with middleware.RequireRole("admin"); head moved it to /api/v2/admin/roles as a bare HandlerFunc with no authz wrapper, so role mutation is no longer admin-gated.
